data.text/markdown:
Camera models and lens distortion

This notebook uses the MRPT Python wheel (pip install mrpt3) to explore pinhole camera models with lens distortion, and their effect on images and on depth-camera point clouds:
  • mrpt.img: camera intrinsics and distortion (TCamera, DistortionModel), images (CImage) and colormaps (colormap()).
  • mrpt.obs: depth images (CObservation3DRangeScan), turned into 3D points by unprojectInto(), which undistorts every pixel with the TCamera model.
A camera inside a corridor with checkered walls takes an image and a depth image. Move the sliders: change the distortion model, the focal length and the distortion coefficients, and see what happens to the image and to the 3D point cloud when the distortion is ignored.

1. The camera model

A 3D point ||((x, y, z)||) in the camera frame (||(z||) forward, ||(y||) down) is first projected onto the normalized plane, ||((x/z,\ y/z)||), then distorted by the lens model, and finally scaled by the focal length and shifted by the principal point: ||(u = f_x x_d + c_x||), ||(v = f_y y_d + c_y||). MRPT supports three distortion models:
  • none: an ideal pinhole camera (or an already rectified image).
  • plumb_bob: the radial-tangential model also used by OpenCV and ROS. Radial coefficients ||(k_1, k_2||) bend straight lines into barrels (negative ||(k_1||)) or pincushions (positive ||(k_1||)); ||(p_1, p_2||) model a lens not parallel to the sensor.
  • kannala_brandt: a fisheye model, a polynomial in the angle ||(\theta||) between the ray and the optical axis. With all its coefficients at zero it is an equidistant fisheye, ||(r_d = \theta||), with a much wider field of view than a pinhole camera of the same focal length.

2. What the camera sees

CObservation3DRangeScan.unprojectInto() converts each pixel of a depth image into a 3D point, undistorting the pixel with the TCamera model. A depth image of 1 m everywhere thus gives the viewing ray of every pixel. We cast those rays against the corridor (NumPy) to render the image and the depth image the camera would capture. Both are stored in CImage objects, annotated with MRPT drawing functions, and the depth is colored with an MRPT colormap.

data.text/markdown:
3. From a depth image to a point cloud

Depth cameras deliver an image like the one above, and unprojectInto() turns it into a point cloud using the camera intrinsics. Below, the same depth image is unprojected twice: with the right model, and with the distortion ignored (as with an uncalibrated camera). Each pixel keeps its depth, but its ray is wrong, so points move sideways: walls seen at an angle and the floor bend, and the corridor shrinks or grows. With the none model both clouds are identical.

data.text/html: Ignoring the distortion moves the points by 2.9 cm on average, and up to 10.2 cm (76,800 points).
